Glossary

Public Records Glossary

Plain-English definitions of terms you will meet when searching court, property, business, and bankruptcy records. Each term links to a guide with more detail.

ACDEFGJLMPRSTU

A

Apostille
A certificate that authenticates a public document so it can be used in another country that belongs to the Hague Apostille Convention. Read more
Assessor
The county official who values property for tax purposes and keeps the ownership information shown on the tax roll. Read more

C

Certified copy
A copy of a record that the office holding the original has stamped, sealed, or signed to confirm that it is a true copy. Read more
Chapter 13
A form of bankruptcy in which an individual with regular income repays some or all debts through a court-approved plan over three to five years. Read more
Chapter 7
A form of bankruptcy in which a trustee may sell nonexempt assets to pay creditors, and eligible debts can be discharged. Read more
Clerk of court
The office that keeps case files, dockets, judgments, and orders for a court and processes new filings. Read more
Complaint
The document that begins a civil lawsuit by stating the plaintiff’s claims against the defendant. Read more

D

Default judgment
A judgment entered for the plaintiff when the defendant does not respond to a lawsuit in time. Read more
Discharge
A court order in bankruptcy that releases a debtor from personal liability for eligible debts. Read more
Disposition
The outcome of a case, such as dismissed, convicted, acquitted, settled, or judgment entered. Read more
Docket
A chronological list of the filings, orders, and events in a court case. Read more

E

Expungement
A court process that removes or seals certain records of an arrest or conviction. Eligibility rules differ by state. Read more

F

FOIA
The Freedom of Information Act, a federal law that lets anyone request records from federal executive branch agencies. Read more

G

Grantor and grantee
In land records, the grantor is the seller or transferor and the grantee is the buyer or recipient named in a deed. Read more

J

Judgment lien
A claim against a debtor’s property that is created when a court judgment is recorded against it. Read more

L

Lien
A legal claim against property that secures payment of a debt. Read more
Lis pendens
A recorded notice that a lawsuit affecting a particular property has been filed. Read more

M

Mechanic’s lien
A lien filed by a contractor or supplier who says they were not paid for work on a property. Read more

P

PACER
Public Access to Court Electronic Records, the federal judiciary’s system for dockets and documents from federal courts. Read more
Plaintiff and defendant
In a civil case, the plaintiff brings the lawsuit and the defendant is the party being sued. Read more
Preponderance of the evidence
The standard of proof in most civil cases, meaning that something is more likely true than not. Read more

R

Recorder or register of deeds
The county office that records deeds, mortgages, liens, and similar land documents and keeps the index used to search them. Read more
Registered agent
The person or company designated to receive legal papers and official notices on behalf of a business. Read more

S

Sealed record
A court record that has been closed to public access by court order. Read more
Secretary of State
In most states, the office that keeps business entity filings and UCC filings. Read more
Service of process
The formal delivery of legal papers, such as a summons and complaint, to a party in a lawsuit. Read more

T

Title search
A review of the recorded history of a property to confirm who owns it and what claims exist against it. Read more

U

UCC filing
A public notice, usually filed with the Secretary of State, that a lender has a security interest in a borrower’s personal property or business assets. Read more

Definitions are general explanations, not legal advice. Terms and procedures can differ by state.
